title: Survivorship Bias
summary: We systematically overestimate success rates because we only study survivors — the failures are invisible. WWII bomber analysis revealed this when engineers wanted to armor the bullet holes they could see, not the ones that brought planes down.
opening_trap: If successful people all share certain habits, does that mean adopting those habits will make you successful?

title: Hedonic Treadmill
summary: Humans rapidly adapt to positive or negative life changes and return to a stable baseline of happiness. Winning the lottery and becoming paralyzed produce surprisingly similar long-term happiness levels.
opening_trap: If nothing you achieve can permanently raise your happiness baseline, is the pursuit of goals fundamentally irrational?

title: Dunning-Kruger Effect
summary: People with limited knowledge in a domain massively overestimate their competence, while genuine experts tend to underestimate theirs. Incompetence prevents accurate self-assessment.
opening_trap: If the most confident person in the room is statistically more likely to be the least informed, why do we keep electing confident leaders?

title: Tragedy of the Commons
summary: Shared resources are inevitably over-exploited when individuals act in rational self-interest. Each actor's individually rational decision leads to a collectively irrational outcome.
opening_trap: If every fisherman fishing sustainably depends on every other fisherman doing the same, what actually stops the ocean from being emptied?

title: Opportunity Cost
summary: Every choice you make implicitly rejects all other available choices. The real cost of any decision is the value of the best forgone alternative — not what you paid.
opening_trap: You took this job over another that paid more. Does that mean you are, by definition, working for less than you're worth?

title: Overton Window
summary: At any given time, only a narrow band of policy ideas are considered politically acceptable. The window shifts not by politicians adopting fringe ideas, but by public discourse normalizing them first.
opening_trap: If ideas that were radical 20 years ago are mainstream today, does that mean there are currently 'crazy' ideas that your grandchildren will consider obvious?

title: Hanlon's Razor
summary: Never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by incompetence. Most institutional failures are coordination problems, not conspiracies.
opening_trap: If we consistently explain bad outcomes as incompetence rather than intent, does that let genuinely malicious actors operate with perfect cover?

title: Goodhart's Law
summary: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. The metric that was tracking real value starts being optimized directly, hollowing out the underlying thing it was meant to represent.
opening_trap: If a school is judged by its exam pass rate, and it starts teaching only to the exam — is it still a school?
